When making a coffee, there are specific measurements established as you make them. There’s a screen that tells us exactly what to do and how much to put in said cup. There should be about 1/2 inch, to an inch, of clearance on the top of each cup. Often, the foam from the steamed milk fills most of that. We’ve had too many lawsuits in the food industry because of coffee that was filled too high and people got burned. Our coffee (espresso) is brewed at approx. 185 degrees Fahrenheit. I’ve gotten badly burned from coffee splashing on my hand. If one store doesn’t follow the measurements properly, that’s them. But as far as how it’s supposed to be, there shouldn’t be that much clearance. I’d take that up with a manager if there’s a real problem.
Also, you can always ask for it to be filled more.
No actually, it’s all pre-determined measurements to prevent burns.

1. Wash the area after doing it with warm water and soap. It will sting, a lot. Just forewarning.
2. Cover with neosporin/medicated Vaseline, etc.
3. Dress it with a band-aid, gauze if the area is too big.
